findings.title: SDK error outputs lose failure status before measured scoring

evidence.detail: Logs output.type=error and writes a debug artifact, then continues.
Returns a normal RunnerResult without an error/outcome field.
RunnerResult cannot represent failure or incomplete completion.
The outer error field is set only when an exception is thrown.
Measured filtering treats any run without error as valid, subject only to judge synthetic status.

findings.trigger: OpenbuffClient.run resolves with output.type=error instead of rejecting; a judge still returns structured scores.
findings.consequence: Provider/runtime failure can be classified as a measured, error-free task. In the new fake-client probe, an injected SDK provider failure became scored 9/10 with measuredRunCount=1 and retained $0.25 cost.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a typed runner outcome carrying SDK error/incomplete/cancelled states; propagate it to EvalRun and keep task outcome separate from judge availability. Preserve partial diff, duration and cost instead of converting unavailable outcomes to success or free failure.
findings.acceptanceProbe: Inject SDK error output, step-limit exhaustion, and cancellation into the real CodebuffRunner->runTask seam; assert task outcome remains failed/incomplete, that measured-success metrics exclude it, and that partial effects/cost persist.

Repository cleanup follows evaluator callback settlement.

findings.trigger: A final check starts a background compiler/test child, then the task is cancelled or its check deadline expires.
findings.consequence: A cancelled receipt can be emitted while test/build processes continue mutating files, consuming resources, or holding pipes. A safe fixture child wrote an owned marker after the check returned cancelled/130; the probe killed that child in finally.
findings.suggestedFix: Use supervised process-tree execution for final checks, with TERM/grace/KILL and drain/reap settlement; separate requested cancellation from proven process termination. Reuse the canonical existing supervisor when available.
findings.acceptanceProbe: Run a fixture shell with a TERM-ignoring/background child that writes a marker after the deadline. Require cancelled/timed_out output only after the entire owned tree is reaped, no late marker, bounded grace, and readable captured diagnostics.

findings.title: Probe-only binary smoke accepts known fatal output

evidence.detail: Capture records fatal patterns on probe stdout/stderr.
requireProbe returns success for code=0 and markerHit without checking fatalHit.
Probe-only mode returns before the full TUI negative fatal gate.
Legacy macOS release validation explicitly selects probe-only mode.

findings.trigger: A packaged native probe reports the expected success marker and exits zero while also printing a known fatal/unhandled rejection.
findings.consequence: The legacy/probe-only release gate can accept contradictory startup evidence. The safe shell fixture emitted Unhandled rejection plus both success markers: probe-only exited 0, whereas the same fixture's full smoke exited 1 after detecting the fatal. These are adversarial harness probes, not evidence about a current installed release binary.
findings.suggestedFix: Require absence of captured fatal markers on every successful probe; settle after stdout/stderr drain and preserve timeout/spawn/error distinctions. Keep full-boot positive checks and bounded capture.
findings.acceptanceProbe: Run a fake binary emitting success+fatal, success-only, missing marker, nonzero exit and late/split fatal output. Both probe-only and full modes must reject every fatal case.

domainAssessment.security: Benchmark setup/final checks inherit the controller environment and home; dummy canary confirmed inheritance, without reading real keys. Install argv and normal/judge filename sanitization are useful but not OS isolation or a prompt-injection proof. Raw runner debug paths still escape. Full-access body behavior is intentional and preserved; eval-task trust is a distinct boundary.
domainAssessment.correctness: Highest concern is outcome truth: resolved SDK error can score as measured success; final-check descendants outlive cancellation. Comparison overwrites repeat populations, finite gates fail open, identifier fidelity is overclaimed, and installed-probe success can contradict fatal output. Typed judge validation, synthetic status and hard score caps are existing strengths.
domainAssessment.state-mutation: Shared persistent lesson test cleanup is destructive; raw debug artifacts and minute-run directories have ownership/containment defects. The normal trace entry is correctly bound per agent and build native loader patch cycles are locked. Test isolation must protect filesystem sinks, not only module state.
domainAssessment.error-handling: Some task/judge/check states are explicit, but SDK output errors, setup failures, aborted process trees and artifact write failures are not consistently settled. Extractor/judge timeouts do not pass abort signals in inspected calls. CI test retries and wrapper staged-update/backoff paths are real; they do not replace typed evaluator status.
domainAssessment.performance: Bounded check concurrency, batched context reads and real benchmark parity/cap/child-reap contracts are useful. CI scaled perf test is mostly completion/positive-time assurance, with selected pathological absolute guards. No comparable end-to-end success/latency/cost/heap or per-language efficiency envelope was established; unknown cost still enters numeric aggregates as 0 at runner warning boundary.
domainAssessment.dependency-hygiene: Bun 1.3.5 and main action SHAs/frozen installs are pinned. Provenance reconciles declared exact and range-resolved upstream record identities, integrity, license and deprecation offline, but is not independent upstream attestation and its update gate is self-blocking. Several release/Rust action tags float. Public SDK externals are manifest-driven; legacy Nx dependency is type-only and executor is unwired, not a proven runtime undeclared-dependency defect.
domainAssessment.test-coverage: 58 safe statistics/proposal/fidelity tests passed; new fake-client, cancellation, NaN, identifier, comparison and smoke probes exposed gaps they do not assert. Destructive lesson tests were not run. Golden calibration replays canned scores into fake clients, so it proves plumbing/clamping, not live judge agreement/injection resistance. Real packed SDK/CLI/native installed tasks and actual GitHub predicate execution remain unknown.
domainAssessment.api-contract: RunnerResult lacks error/outcome; task language fields disappear at output; model/cost units and resolved route/version provenance are insufficient for trustworthy comparisons. SDK dual ESM/CJS/type conditions and selected Node exports are explicit and wired. Root SCM preload removal matches current filesystem query loading; no current import break was found. Supplemental CLI npm wrapper manifest is context-only outside pinned inventory.

coverageLimits: All 18 required bounded picker sections were read exactly; secondary/adjacent sections are explicitly recorded in readRanges. No whole-file audit or untouched-source correctness guarantee is implied.
Structural receipt includes only current pinned inventory members actually read; supplemental cli/release/index.js/package.json remain excluded.

No provider/model call, network action, installer, build, publish, real credentials, private home config, old eval logs/traces or private dataset was intentionally inspected or executed. One broad JSON consumer search accidentally matched historical error text; it was discarded, unarchived and unused, and all subsequent searches were restricted to source/YAML/exact public fixtures/manifests.
The safe injected runner intentionally redirected its otherwise unsafe debug path to this shard's owned temporary fixture; no source fixes or unrelated writes were made.

Initial Node fake-binary output capture was empty in this environment; the fatal-gate conclusion uses the successful independently captured shell fixture. This is not a finding about the installed Node/CLI runtime.

No real package/tarball/native artifact or complete GitHub run was executed. Matrix booleans versus string guards and stale Rust exec-stub smoke are pair09-owned; static workflow reads alone do not establish whether GitHub ran those predicates.

Runtime mutation safety is pair06; memory store/retention behavior is pair04; concrete query/grammar packaging omissions are pair07. This shard evaluates their oracle/learning/installed-assurance boundaries and avoids duplicate defects.
Unsafe run-buffbench.test.ts was deliberately not executed because its cleanup deletes shared persistent lessons. The root agent was notified before any broad eval package run.

No inferred advantage or completeness claim is made for implementation-language migration or generic polyglot grammars. The ready queue repairs deterministic TS outcomes first and requires target-language/cross-language task evidence before adoption.

recommendedPlanWork.title: Make evaluator outcomes trustworthy before any adoption
recommendedPlanWork.currentProblem: 11-F1/F2/F3 allow false success, late work and destructive test cleanup.
recommendedPlanWork.smallestScope: Typed task/setup/runner outcomes, supervised final-check lifecycle and injected lesson/artifact roots inside current evaluator TS files.
recommendedPlanWork.languageDecision: Repair in TypeScript; reuse current runtime supervisor rather than awaiting a Python/Rust rewrite.
behavioralAcceptanceProbes: SDK error/incomplete/cancelled retains failed outcome with partial cost/diff.
Entire check process tree reaped before result settlement.
Seeded unrelated lesson sentinel survives each proposal test.
regressionChecks: Existing graph order/skipped/configuration/timeouts and synthetic-versus-measured score assertions.
recommendedPlanWork.observableCompletionEvidence: Key-free integration receipts for each failure state; shared-data tests are safe to run.
recommendedPlanWork.stopOrDeferRule: Do not launch broad eval suites or candidate learning while shared sinks/process settlement remain unsafe.

recommendedPlanWork.title: Emit immutable repeat- and language-aware comparison evidence
recommendedPlanWork.currentProblem: 11-F4/F5/F6/F9/F10 undermine populations, provenance, valid statistics and run ownership.
recommendedPlanWork.smallestScope: One experiment/run/artifact identity schema, exclusive artifact writer, actual resolved model/settings capture, common finite/statistical filtering and wired strata output.
recommendedPlanWork.languageDecision: TypeScript contracts and current statistical helpers; no ML service needed.
behavioralAcceptanceProbes: Input-order-invariant repeats preserve measured zero/low scores and per-agent failures.
Cross-repo identical SHAs never pair accidentally.
Manifest-only reconstruction yields exact per-language/repeat counts and model config provenance.
regressionChecks: Bootstrap determinism/ties/underpowered cases; crash trace and reserved-key protections.
recommendedPlanWork.observableCompletionEvidence: Fresh-fixture comparison shows -3.25 rather than +1.00, plus immutable compatible manifest and stratum receipts.
recommendedPlanWork.stopOrDeferRule: Reject incompatible/underpowered manifests; do not infer missing model/language labels or count repeats as independent task strata.

recommendedPlanWork.title: Graduate correctness and continuation oracles
recommendedPlanWork.currentProblem: 11-F7 identifier fidelity, optional mutable check commands and injected-only summaries cannot prove task or memory correctness.
recommendedPlanWork.smallestScope: Independent value/constraint/blocker truth oracles and protected held-out validation; deterministic real SDK mutation/continuation integration over public polyglot fixtures.
recommendedPlanWork.languageDecision: Keep TS evaluator; use existing target-language compilers/tests and existing Rust protocol, not another language host.
behavioralAcceptanceProbes: Wrong value with right path fails; aged/restarted continuation retains required facts.
An intentionally wrong implementation is rejected by an immutable oracle even if it edits visible tests.
One task changes an interface and validates TS/Python/Rust consumers with versions, byte/position encoding, cancellation and effect receipts.
regressionChecks: Keep F1 non-vacuous eviction, F3 exact recall, retention floors and edit transport injection assertions.
recommendedPlanWork.observableCompletionEvidence: Held-out fixture manifest with independent failure controls and per-language/cross-boundary validation receipts.
recommendedPlanWork.stopOrDeferRule: Do not call summary quality, grammar count or generic shell coverage semantic polyglot competence; defer unsupported ecosystems explicitly.

recommendedPlanWork.title: Wire a reviewed candidate learning channel
recommendedPlanWork.currentProblem: Current extraction is optional and adoption/routing is absent; playbook counters and lessons are not held-out improvement.
recommendedPlanWork.smallestScope: Candidate definition artifact in a separate worktree/channel, controlled baseline/candidate held-out runs, validated decisions, explicit adoption pointer and rollback record; keep default route human-configured until evidence passes.
recommendedPlanWork.languageDecision: TS orchestration first. Consider Python ML only after sufficient trustworthy independent observations demonstrate a concrete estimator/routing advantage.
behavioralAcceptanceProbes: No candidate may pass without independent paired held-out evidence and correctness/resource budgets.
Non-applied/skipped/unsafe proposals are typed; model/tool/budget changes validate against actual runtime contracts.
Accepted candidate changes one explicit consumer; rejected candidate leaves active pointer unchanged; rollback restores prior pointer.
regressionChecks: Zero-delta/missing-pair live rejection, no implicit apply, legal handleSteps clone/serialization fixtures and playbook reporter isolation.
recommendedPlanWork.observableCompletionEvidence: Before/after artifact manifests, stratum confidence intervals, efficiency/success tradeoff report, adopted consumer and rollback receipts.
recommendedPlanWork.stopOrDeferRule: If evidence is underpowered, contaminated or worse in required strata, reject/defer; never graduate a dry run or unconsumed helper.

recommendedPlanWork.title: Verify what is packed and installed
recommendedPlanWork.currentProblem: Repository-local dist imports and injected wrapper tests do not prove external SDK/CLI/native consumer behavior.
recommendedPlanWork.smallestScope: Install the exact produced SDK tarball/CLI archive plus wrapper into fresh temporary consumers outside workspace ancestry; provider-free task probes on declared engine/platform lanes; verify native host protocol consumer in CI.
recommendedPlanWork.languageDecision: Keep Node/Bun TS host and existing Rust sidecar; use native OS runners for executable ABI proof.
behavioralAcceptanceProbes: Import both SDK conditions at declared Node minimum and current supported Node; deterministic read/edit/validate/cancel task succeeds with production deps only.
CLI wrapper installs exact checksummed archive, boots and executes a native/grammar task without source-tree fallback.
Success+fatal fake probes fail in every mode; native tests and smoke execute on intended lanes.
regressionChecks: ESM fixup selected/all public export coverage, strict declaration checks, offline wrapper healing/rollback and release commit/tag provenance.
recommendedPlanWork.observableCompletionEvidence: Tarball/archive hashes, dependency graph, runtime versions and real installed task/protocol receipts attached to exact release commit.
recommendedPlanWork.stopOrDeferRule: No release completion on only --version, copied dist, injected probe or skipped native lane; unsupported targets must be explicit.

recommendedPlanWork.title: Align release governance and efficiency gates with actual guarantees
recommendedPlanWork.currentProblem: 11-F11 blocks legitimate provenance updates; perf smoke has no general task/latency/cost regression envelope; local/remote schedules differ.
recommendedPlanWork.smallestScope: Approved provenance update policy and event-base fixture tests; explicit guard/test schedule coverage; stable baseline resource budgets with noise-aware regression decisions and artifact provenance.
recommendedPlanWork.languageDecision: TS guard changes and current CI; no additional executor ecosystem unless measured need exists.
behavioralAcceptanceProbes: Approved new release entries pass while unauthorized existing identities fail across PR/push ranges.
An intentional after-path slowdown outside the declared budget fails the numeric gate.
Zero discovery, skipped native steps and retries are visible in a coverage/failure receipt.
regressionChecks: Retain frozen Bun pins, exact/range provenance integrity/license/deprecation checks and structural performance contracts.
recommendedPlanWork.observableCompletionEvidence: Executed guard policy fixture matrix and budgeted comparable workload results with dispersion; actual CI receipts when authorized.
recommendedPlanWork.stopOrDeferRule: Defer broad performance claims without stable workload/baseline. Retire/defer unused build-tools surfaces until a real consumer justifies tests/maintenance.
